name: Pyroclastic Rubric
description: Pyroclastic Rubric is a medium-sized volcanic world where the rules of geological violence are written in red. Its surface is organized into distinct zones of destruction—tectonic rift valleys that split continents, supervolcanic calderas that reshape the landscape on decadal timescales, and acid rain regions where sulfuric precipitation has carved the rock into fantastical spire formations. The magnetic poles wander erratically, completing full reversals every few centuries and disrupting navigation in ways that have been painstakingly charted and re-charted.

The sky above Pyroclastic Rubric is a perpetual twilight of ash and chemical haze, lit from below by the glow of active lava flows that create an eerie, ruddy illumination. The acid rain falls in predictable seasonal patterns, and the periods between falls are marked by an unsettling clarity—the toxic atmosphere briefly thinning enough to reveal a star field stained amber by residual particulates. The ground vibrates constantly, a subsonic pulse that experienced surveyors learn to read like a seismograph.

A platinum mining operation ran here for forty years, extracting extraordinary quantities of rare metals from the rift valley deposits before a series of eruptions destroyed the primary processing facility and killed seventeen workers. The abandoned complex still stands partially buried in cooite lava, its surviving structures slowly being consumed by the planet's geology. Microbial life was discovered in the mine's deepest shafts, subsisting on chemical energy in conditions of extreme heat and acidity.

The microbes of Pyroclastic Rubric are endangered by the radiation hotspots that have intensified near the mine site—whether from natural geological processes or contamination from the mining operation's nuclear power systems remains disputed. The platinum deposits remain among the richest known, and proposals to resume extraction surface periodically. Each time, the planet answers with another eruption, another rift, another rewriting of the rubric that governs what can and cannot be taken from its burning pages.
